case: Our online store makes most of its revenue through checkout. Last month checkout went down for 25 minutes during a campaign, and Black Friday is in six weeks with up to 3 times normal traffic. Leadership wants to know whether we're ready, what it will cost to be ready, and how we'll know in real time if something breaks.

questions.q: Tell me about a system you kept running that made money directly. How did you find out what an hour of downtime cost the business?
questions.deep: Who gave you that number, and how did it change your priorities?
questions.expect: Knows revenue per minute or a proxy, got it from finance or product, and used it to prioritize.

questions.q: Before touching anything for Black Friday, what would you ask product and finance about our checkout?
questions.deep: Which of those answers would change your plan the most?
questions.expect: Asks peak traffic, revenue per hour, campaigns and acceptable degradation: why before how.

questions.q: Tell me about an SLO you defined with a business owner. How did you choose the target?
questions.deep: What happened the first time you burned the error budget?
questions.expect: Target tied to customer experience and the cost of each extra nine; business owner involved.

questions.q: In our case, which parts of checkout can degrade on Black Friday and which can never fail? How do you decide?
questions.deep: Who signs off on that list?
questions.expect: Separates the payment path from nice-to-haves, decides with product, plans graceful degradation.

questions.q: Leadership gives you budget for one thing before Black Friday: more capacity, a load test or better alerts. Which one and why?
questions.deep: What do we lose with the options you didn't choose?
questions.expect: Compares cost against revenue at risk per hour; picks with data; names what stays uncovered.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you chose between scaling up and fixing the root cause under time pressure. What did each option cost?
questions.deep: Looking back, was it the right call? What would you change?
questions.expect: Weighs cost, time and risk explicitly, decides consciously and follows up on the debt.

questions.q: Our database is the bottleneck at 2 times traffic. How would you reach 3 times in six weeks, and how would you explain the cost to leadership?
questions.deep: What's the cheapest option that still protects revenue?
questions.expect: Options with cost and risk (replicas, cache, queues, limits), picks with data, one-line business case.

questions.q: Tell me about a cloud cost you reduced without hurting customers. How did you prove it didn't?
questions.deep: What was the saving per month and what did you watch after the change?
questions.expect: Saving in money, before/after metrics, guardrails and evidence that customers weren't affected.

questions.q: Tell me about the worst incident you handled. What did it cost the business, and what did you do in the first 15 minutes?
questions.deep: What did you tell leadership and customers, and when?
questions.expect: Real case, own actions, stops the bleeding first, communicates early, impact quantified.

questions.q: It's Black Friday, 9 pm, and checkout errors are at 8%. Walk me through your next 30 minutes.
questions.deep: When do you roll back without knowing the cause?
questions.expect: Mitigates before diagnosing, clear rollback criteria, roles and comms cadence; protects revenue.

questions.q: Tell me about a postmortem that changed how the company works, not only the code.
questions.deep: How did you make sure the action items actually happened?
questions.expect: Blameless, business impact stated, a systemic change, owners and dates followed up.

questions.q: How would you load-test checkout at 3 times traffic without risking real customers or real payments?
questions.deep: What result would make you tell leadership we're not ready?
questions.expect: Production-like test, payment sandbox, ramp plan and a go/no-go threshold tied to the business.

questions.q: Tell me about reliability work whose value you had to prove. What number did you show, and to whom?
questions.deep: How did you turn minutes saved into money or customers?
questions.expect: Climbs from output to outcome to impact: incidents and MTTR into downtime avoided and revenue.

questions.q: After Black Friday, which three numbers would you report to show the preparation was worth it?
questions.deep: Which of them would the CFO care about most?
questions.expect: Availability at peak, failed orders or revenue protected, cost of preparing; compared with last year.

questions.q: Tell me about toil you automated. How many hours did it free, and what did the team do with them?
questions.deep: How did you measure those hours?
questions.expect: Hours measured before and after and reinvested in valuable work, not just 'I automated X'.

questions.q: How would you know in real time that Black Friday is going well for the business, not only for the servers?
questions.deep: Which alert would wake you up?
questions.expect: Business metrics on screen (orders per minute, payment success); alerts on customer impact, not CPU.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you asked for budget or people for reliability. How did you make the case?
questions.deep: What did you say the business would lose without it?
questions.expect: Risk of not doing it in money or customers, a clear ask, alternatives and the real outcome.

questions.q: Leadership asks 'Are we ready for Black Friday?' and you're not sure. What do you answer?
questions.deep: How do you say 'not yet' without sounding like a blocker?
questions.expect: Honest status with risks, what's needed and by when, options; no false confidence.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you said no to a launch or a change for reliability reasons. How did it end?
questions.deep: What did you offer instead?
questions.expect: Explains the risk in business terms, offers conditions or an alternative, keeps the relationship.

questions.q: How would you explain a 25-minute checkout outage to the sales team in two sentences?
questions.deep: What would you never say to them?
questions.expect: Plain words: what happened, the impact, what changed. No jargon, no blame, no excuses.
